label: def:hyperelliptic-quintic
title: The hyperelliptic quintic $\mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1$
html:
Definition. The hyperelliptic quintic \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1

Let \mathcal{X}_5 denote the smooth projective completion of the affine curve

  \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 =  x^5 - 1
  \qquad
  \text{in } \mathbb{A}^2(\mathbb{C}).

We view \mathcal{X}_5 as a double cover of \mathbb{P}^1 via the projection (x, y) \mapsto x. Writing \zeta_5 = e^{2\pi i/5} for a primitive fifth root of unity, the ramification locus of this double cover consists of the six branch points

  \{x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4, \infty\}  =
   \{1, \zeta_5, \zeta_5^2, \zeta_5^3, \zeta_5^4, \infty\}.

Five distribute symmetrically on the unit circle; the last lies at infinity. By Riemann–Hurwitz, the genus of \mathcal{X}_5 is

  g(\mathcal{X}_5)  =  \frac{6 - 2}{2}  =  2.

Thus \mathcal{X}_5 is a hyperelliptic Riemann surface of genus 2 in the Bolza family [bolza1887]. Its hyperelliptic involution is \iota \colon (x, y) \mapsto (x, -y).

Relation to Bring's surface. The coordinate x on \mathcal{X}_5 is a \mathbb{Z}_5-equivariant observable. We identify it with the first Lagrange resolvent w_1 of prop:lagrange-resolvent-transform, restricted to the cyclic subgroup \mathbb{Z}_5 \subset S_5 of Bring's surface. Under this identification, the five branch points \zeta_5^k are the cyclic images of a single \mathbb{Z}_5-orbit.
